title: Sentence Similarity III
statement:
A *sentence* is one or more words joined by single spaces, with no space at either end; each word is made of uppercase and lowercase English letters. Two sentences are *similar* when one of them can be turned into the other by adding a run of zero or more whole words at one single place in it: before its first word, between two of its words, or after its last word. The added words must stay separate words, so nothing may be glued onto an existing word.

Given `sentence1` and `sentence2`, return `true` if they are similar and `false` otherwise. Words are compared exactly, so case matters.
constraints: sentence1 and sentence2 contain only uppercase letters, lowercase letters and spaces
words are separated by a single space, with no leading or trailing spaces
notes:
## Intuition

Words can only be added to the sentence with fewer words. If that happens at one place, the shorter sentence must equal some words from the start of the longer one followed by some words from its end. A brute force tries every block of words to cut out of the longer sentence, which is cubic. Two pointers do it directly: match as many words as possible from the front, then from the back, and see whether together they cover the whole shorter sentence.

## Approach

1. Split both sentences into words and name the one with fewer words `shorter`, the other `longer`.
2. `gap` is how many words the longer one has extra; the `k`-th word from the back of `shorter` lines up with index `k + gap` in `longer`.
3. Move `left` forward while `shorter[left]` equals `longer[left]`.
4. Move `right` backward while `shorter[right]` equals `longer[right + gap]`, never crossing `left`.
5. The sentences are similar exactly when the pointers have crossed (`left > right`): every word of `shorter` is in the matched prefix or suffix.

## Example 1, step by step

`shorter = ["My", "Haley"]`, `longer = ["My", "name", "is", "Haley"]`, `gap = 2`. From the front, `My` matches, `left` becomes `1`; `Haley` does not equal `name`, so it stops. From the back, `right = 1`: `Haley` equals `longer[3]`, so `right` becomes `0`. Now `left = 1 > right = 0`, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m) for splitting and one pass of each pointer, where n and m are the sentence lengths.
- Space: O(n + m) for the word arrays.

## Pitfalls

- Compare whole words, not characters: `"Frog cool"` and `"Frogs are cool"` share the text `Frog` but not the word.
- Stop the back pointer at `left`, or the same word is counted twice, as in `"a b a"` against `"a"`.
- Sentences with the same number of words are similar only when they are equal.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `shorter`, `longer` | the two sentences' words, fewer words first |
| `gap` | extra word count of `longer` |
| `left` | number of words matched from the front |
| `right` | last unmatched index of `shorter` while matching from the back |
